 Live .  7,562 viewing 7562 viewing England openers start well against Sri Lanka
 Thu 29 Oct 2026 , Men's One Day International Series Sri Lanka vs England (batting), in play Sri Lanka Sri Lanka In Play England England Yet to bat 54 -0 ( 8.4 ) England are 54 for 0 with 41.2 overs remaining Sri Lanka: yet to bat England innings: 54 for 0 from 8.4 overs, in play
 Live Reporting (active) 
 Scorecard 
 Summary
 Sri Lanka win toss and bowl first in Lahore
 England already eliminated from tri-series
 Close form Have your say on England men this winter
 Get involved Live Reporting
 by Ffion Wynne
 South Africa v Australia under way published at 08:41 GMT 08:41 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Play has started over in Cape Town, where Australia resume on day three with a small first-innings lead and six wickets in hand.
 Josh Inglis and Alex Carey are close to a 150-run partnership having come together at 185-4.
 You can follow that match on our dedicated live page .
 0 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 08:39 GMT 08:39 GMT 
 Steven Finn 
Former England fast bowler on BBC Test Match Special 
 England are looking good, but they will be wary that 429 is not enough, so they will have to keep going. 
 13 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 52-0 published at 8 overs 8 overs 
 Duckett 30, Banton 21 
 Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis senses the need for a change, so here's an early look at the left-arm spin of Dunith Wellalage. 
 He can't stop the flurry of runs, though, as Tom Banton reverse sweeps nicely to the boundary. 
 10 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 08:36 GMT 08:36 GMT 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 Nine off the over has got England motoring.
 22 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 46-0 published at 7 overs 7 overs 
 England are ticking along very nicely now. 
 Duckett drives down the ground for four more. 
 18 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 08:34 GMT 08:34 GMT 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 Image source, Getty Images Lovely shot from Ben Duckett. You know it is a good shot when nobody in the ring bothers moving. 
 15 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 42-0 published at 6.4 overs 6.4 overs 
 Punished! 
 Asitha Fernando has been Sri Lanka's most consistent seamer so far this morning but this is a freebie, short and wide outside the off stump and Ben Duckett hammers it for four. 
 Oh, and it was a no-ball. That'll be a free hit.
 13 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 08:31 GMT 08:31 GMT 
 Click 'Get Involved' at the top of this page to have your say 
 Why take Crane and Coles if they’re not going to be picked even in a dead rubber. Same old management. Nothing changes.
 Peter, Bergamo 
 I hope he proves me wrong but I feel Crocombe has been given a hospital pass. He is an excellent red ball bowler but didn't pull up any trees in white ball cricket for Sussex. It would be sad if his international prospects hinge on these games.
 Richard, Bromley 
 32 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 37-0 published at 6 overs 6 overs 
 Image source, Reuters Banton goes back-to-back! He's been rewarded for his patience here. 
 Malinga doesn't do a lot wrong but it's such a good pitch. A good length delivery is simply nudged off the pads and it races away to the ropes. A productive over for England. 
 24 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 08:28 GMT 08:28 GMT 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 Confidence back into Tom Banton's batting with that shot. 
 This time it was timed beautifully into the off side for four.
 21 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 33-0 published at 5.3 overs 5.3 overs 
 Early bowling change for Sri Lanka, as Eshan Malinga replaces Madushanka. 
 And on cue, Tom Banton pings one out of the middle of the bat at last, another backfoot punch past extra cover. 
 17 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 08:26 GMT 08:26 GMT 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 A good fluid start from Ben Duckett and a sticky start from Tom Banton.
 Banton is not timing that shot on the back foot today.
 I can't imagine Banton throwing this wicket away today as we have talked about how important this innings is for him to try to get a game in Australia when Jacob Bethell comes back.
 10 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 27-0 published at 5 overs 5 overs 
 Image source, Reuters More exquisite timing from Duckett, who plays a defensive prod that still flies through the covers and they're able to scamper back for three, and then clips into the leg side for a couple more.
 Tom Banton, on the other hand, still looks a little scratchy but Duckett's fluency is taking the pressure off him for now. 
 17 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 08:19 GMT 08:19 GMT 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 A lovely shot through the covers from Ben Duckett. 
 He just waits for the ball underneath his eyes, and then punches it through the covers for four. 
 30 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 21-0 published at 4 overs 4 overs 
 Textbook Ben Duckett.
 Back of a length outside the off stump, and he thumps it for four between point and cover, barely moving his feet at all. 
 It's a fresh pitch and the ball isn't doing much. Feels like at least one of England's openers needs to cash in.
 19 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 14-0 published at 3 overs 3 overs 
 Image source, Reuters Shot. 
 It's the first loose ball from Asitha Fernando, having done so well to keep Tom Banton quiet, but it's a fraction too short and Banton punches beautifully off the back foot for four. 
 25 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 8-0 published at 2 overs 2 overs 
 Back-to-back boundaries for Duckett to get England going, though this one's not quite as convincing as he top-edges a short ball for four more. 
 25 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 08:09 GMT 08:09 GMT 
 Rufus Bullough 
CricViz analyst 
 The new ball has been a much more potent weapon since the tri-series shifted to Lahore.
 Powerplay seam bowlers in this tri-series:
 Rawalpindi - 6 wickets, avg 49.33, SR 57.1
 Lahore - 10 wickets, avg 20.40, SR 23.7
 14 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 4-0 published at 1.4 overs 1.4 overs 
 And England's patience is rewarded.
 Madushanka drifts on to the pads and Ben Duckett doesn't miss out, whipping the ball past square leg for four. Lovely timing.
 26 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 0-0 published at 1.3 overs 1.3 overs 
 Very good start from Dilshan Madushanka, too. 
 Nine balls without a run for England...
